checks.claim: At a treatment plant, bar screens catch rags and trash before the sewage reaches the tanks.
checks.why: EPA: screening is the first unit operation at treatment plants and removes rags, paper, plastics and metals to prevent damage and clogging downstream.

sources.title: EPA fact sheet: Screening and grit removal

checks.claim: In a primary settling tank, heavy solids sink to the bottom and scum floats to the top.
checks.why: Primary clarifiers slow the flow so heavy solids settle as primary sludge while grease and scum float and are skimmed.

checks.claim: In an aeration tank, blown-in air feeds bacteria that eat the dissolved waste.
checks.why: In activated sludge, aeration supplies oxygen to bacteria that oxidize dissolved organic matter into new cells, carbon dioxide and water.

checks.claim: Ultraviolet light is used to kill germs in treated wastewater before it is released.
checks.why: UV disinfection at about 254 nm damages microbes' DNA so bacteria and viruses cannot reproduce; it is used on treated effluent and leaves no chemical residue.
